item.title: Nadi woman's death classified as murder
item.description: The death of a woman in her 20s, whose body was found in Nadi on Thursday, has been classified as murder by Police. Police say her body was discovered near a complex in Nadi.
item.content:encoded:
The death of a woman in her 20s, whose body was found in Nadi on Thursday, has been classified as murder by Police.

Police say her body was discovered near a complex in Nadi.

Meanwhile, the death of a man whose body was found floating in the Labasa River on Friday is yet to be classified, as a post-mortem examination has not been conducted.

Police say investigations into both cases are continuing.

item.title: Police urge parents to monitor children following concerns along Khalsa Road
item.description: Police are urging parents to monitor their children's whereabouts following concerns raised about young people gathering along Khalsa Road in the evenings. A concerned resident has told fijivillage News that children, including girls wearing school uniforms, have been seen in the area after 8pm without adult supervision.
item.content:encoded:
Police are urging parents to monitor their children's whereabouts following concerns raised about young people gathering along Khalsa Road in the evenings.

A concerned resident has told fijivillage News that children, including girls wearing school uniforms, have been seen in the area after 8pm without adult supervision.

The resident also claims some young people have been seen sniffing glue and fighting, raising concerns about their safety.

In response to questions from fijivillage News, Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe has reminded parents and guardians to make their children's safety a priority.

Vusonilawe says parents must know where their children are, who they are spending time with, and ensure they return home safely.

He is also urging parents to make sure their children do not get involved with the wrong crowd.

item.title: No injuries reported after rental car catches fire near Nausori Airport
item.description: No injuries have been reported after a rental car caught fire near the Nausori Airport junction last night. The National Fire Authority confirms that firefighters from Nausori responded to the incident and extinguished the blaze.
item.content:encoded:
No injuries have been reported after a rental car caught fire near the Nausori Airport junction last night.

The National Fire Authority confirms that firefighters from Nausori responded to the incident and extinguished the blaze.

The NFA says the driver was present at the scene when firefighters arrived.

They sas an electrical fault is suspected to have caused the fire.

Questions have been sent to Police for further details on the incident.

item.title: Namara representative calls for GCC recognition, provincial Senate representation and removal of FICAC
item.description: The Mata-ni-Tikina of Namara, Sekaia Mua, is calling for the Great Council of Chiefs to be formally recognised under the proposed constitutional changes, provincial representation in the Senate and the removal of the Fiji Independent Commission Against Corruption. Mua raised these issues while making his submission to the Joint Parliamentary Select Committee on the Constitution (Amendment) Bill 20
item.content:encoded:
The Mata-ni-Tikina of Namara, Sekaia Mua, is calling for the Great Council of Chiefs to be formally recognised under the proposed constitutional changes, provincial representation in the Senate and the removal of the Fiji Independent Commission Against Corruption.

Mua raised these issues while making his submission to the Joint Parliamentary Select Committee on the Constitution (Amendment) Bill 2026 at Vunimono Hall in Nausori.

He says the Great Council of Chiefs plays an important role in protecting iTaukei culture, traditions and the interests of indigenous communities.

Mua believes the removal of the Council in the past weakened the traditional authority and identity of indigenous Fijians, and says its role should be strengthened under the proposed constitutional changes.

He also supports provincial representation in the Senate, saying this would help maintain the traditional chiefly system and ensure provincial voices are represented.

On FICAC, Mua called for the Commission to be removed, arguing that corruption investigations should instead be handled by the Fiji Police Force.

He questioned FICAC's effectiveness and raised concerns about how corruption cases are handled.

Mua also urged the Committee not to rush the proposed referendum, saying people in villages and rural communities must be given enough time to understand the proposed constitutional changes before making a decision.

He says the Government must ensure the concerns of indigenous Fijians are heard and their interests protected when decisions are made about the country's future.

Meanwhile, Mua also highlighted the serious water shortage affecting people in Namara, Tailevu, saying some families have been forced to use a water source previously declared unsafe by the Ministry of Health.

He says villagers have no alternative water supply, while dry conditions continue to affect their access to clean drinking water.

Mua says the Water Authority of Fiji delivered water on one occasion, but no further supplies have been received.

He says residents have been requesting a proper water supply for years and are still waiting for a lasting solution.

Mua, who has served as Mata-ni-Tikina for four years, says villagers continue to ask him when assistance will arrive.

He is calling on the Government and the Water Authority of Fiji to urgently address the shortage, saying rural communities should not be forgotten.

item.title: Elderly Suva couple still fear for safety as faulty streetlight remains unrepaired
item.description: About a month after a series of break-ins at their home, an elderly couple living on Cumming Street in Suva say they still fear for their safety as a streetlight behind their building remains out and responsibility for repairing it remains unclear. Mitesh Sutaria says he has contacted both the Suva City Council and the Fiji Roads Authority about the faulty streetlight along the Terry Walk side of
item.content:encoded:
About a month after a series of break-ins at their home, an elderly couple living on Cumming Street in Suva say they still fear for their safety as a streetlight behind their building remains out and responsibility for repairing it remains unclear.

Mitesh Sutaria says he has contacted both the Suva City Council and the Fiji Roads Authority about the faulty streetlight along the Terry Walk side of their building, but each organisation has referred him to the other.

According to Sutaria, emails he received indicate that FRA considers the streetlight to be SCC's responsibility, while SCC maintains that it falls under FRA.

He says the situation has left him frustrated and confused, particularly as the area remains dark at night.

Sutaria says SCC has repaired a light near the public convenience beside their building, but the streetlight along the footpath behind the property remains out.

He says the lack of lighting is a major safety concern, especially after the break-ins, as people continue to gather around the area, particularly near the public convenience.

Sutaria says he sometimes feels unsafe walking around the area, including when going shopping nearby, because people often gather or sleep along the footpath.

Following the break-ins, he says he has water-blasted and cleaned the area around the building and installed barbed wire along the fence to improve security.

However, Sutaria says he and his wife remain worried that their home could be targeted again and have decided against travelling overseas for the time being because of their safety concerns.

He says he has also not received any major update from Police on the investigation into the break-ins.

Apart from the streetlight, Sutaria has raised concerns with SCC about a strong unpleasant smell coming from the public toilet beside their building.

He says the smell sometimes reaches their home and affects other tenants in the building.

Sutaria says residents pay city rates and expect public facilities to be regularly cleaned and maintained in a hygienic condition.

He is urgently calling on whichever organisation is responsible, SCC or FRA, to repair the streetlight and address the safety concerns of residents.

Questions have again been sent to SCC and FRA to clarify who is responsible for maintaining the streetlight and when it will be repaired.

Police have also been contacted for an update on the investigation into the break-ins.
